newsitem.title: JAPAN: Higher kerosene stocks depress Japanese imports.
newsitem.headline: Higher kerosene stocks depress Japanese imports.

text.p: Replenished kerosene stocks in Japan deterred trading houses from stepping up kerosene imports towards winter, the first heating season since imports of oil products were deregulated in April, traders said on Wednesday.
"With domestic kerosene inventories this high, it would be very difficult to find a buyer of import cargoes," said one middle distillate trader with a trading house.
Japan's kerosene stocks had been substantially lower than year-earlier levels until July, due to refiners' policy of keeping inventories low, as well as colder-than-usual weather last winter.
However, kerosene inventories jumped at the end of August, partly due to higher output by domestic refiners, and this discouraged prospective importers at trading houses.
Firmer spot kerosene import prices are another reason trading houses are thinking twice about importing.
With kerosene prices above $30.00 per barrel on a cost-and-freight basis, imports would end up being more expensive than domestically processed kerosene, traders said.

Since the deregulation, eight non-refiners, mostly trading houses, have acquired licences to import kerosene, traders said. Importing gasoline, kerosene and gas oil was formerly limited to domestic refiners.
